thread:
Alex: quick sync — ran into a confusing interaction between tier-aware AB canaries + smart routing fallback in staging. enterprise users were supposed to hit canary variant but instead got served a quantized fallback. telemetry didn't make it obvious which policy triggered the swap. can we decide how rollout scoping should tie into routing/fallback?

Maria: ugh. do we have logs/traces that show the order?

Chen: short version: routing policy evaluated per-request (region->capacity->tier), decided to use a cheaper variant because pool capacity was low, then rollout evaluation kicked in and matched the canary flag — but runtime then picked fallback model because it was considered "compatible" and cheaper. telemetry only recorded final selected model, not the pre-fallback decision.

Sam: my proposal: make rollout scoping evaluation happen before fallback selection so we can honor exposure intent for a tier. precedence: (1) rollout scoping, (2) routing policy (region/cost), (3) fallback candidate selection. That way the canary exposure stays visible. downside: might slightly change capacity decisions.

Chen: cautious — changing precedence could increase latency on cold paths if rollout decision forces a model that isn't locally available. We need a tiebreaker rather than absolute reorder. e.g. allow routing to choose fallback only if the rollout-exposed model is unavailable AND fallback has acceptable quality delta.

Lisa: from console/UX side, we also need per-tier exposure metrics and a quick flag showing "fallbacks active" per rollout. customers keep asking "did my enterprise canary actually see the new model or not?"

Sam: agreed. a concrete config idea below — this would let users scope rollouts and also express fallback preference. thoughts?

```
{
  "route": "predict",
  "scope": {
    "tiers": ["enterprise", "standard"],
    "regions": ["eu-west-1"]
  },
  "rollout": {
    "type": "ab",
    "exposure": { "enterprise": 0.02, "standard": 0.1 },
    "rollout_id": "canary-2027-04-11"
  },
  "fallback": {
    "fallback_candidates": ["m-1-int8", "m-1-fp16"],
    "preserve_rollout": true,
    "report_reason": true
  }
}
```

Maria: I like preserve_rollout=true by default for per-tier canaries. If runtime can't meet latency/throughput we can still fallback but flag it as "fallback_preserved=false" and emit metrics.

Chen: telemetry needs to include these fields on every request event: rollout_id, tier, fallback_preserved (bool), fallback_reason (enum), selected_model, target_model, latency_ms, token_count. then we can create dashboards like fallback_rate_by_tier and canary_exposure_by_tier.

ops-bot: automated rule suggestion: alert if fallback_rate_by_tier > 1% for 5m for any tier. also log top fallback_reason and top selected_model differences.

Lisa: console change request: in rollouts UX show a per-tier exposure control and a small "fallback activity" panel (sparkline + sample request list). clicking a sample opens a trace with routing decisions and fallback_reason.

Sam: back to runtime semantics — we could implement a tiebreaker that prefers rollout-selected model when preserve_rollout=true, but allows fallback if the selected model isn't in the same capacity pool AND we'd violate latency SLO. fallback_reason should encode "capacity" vs "quality_delta" vs "region_unavailable".

Alex: actionables I think we can agree on:
- telemetry: add rollout_id, tier, fallback_preserved, fallback_reason, selected_model, target_model, latency_ms, token_count (P0)
- runtime: implement tiebreaker honoring preserve_rollout flag, fallback only when SLO or capacity constraints require it (P1)
- console: add per-tier exposure view + fallback activity panel (P1)
- API: prefer explicit fields fallback_candidates + preserve_rollout vs old fallback_model (P2)

Maria: small API debate — do we call it preserve_rollout or prefer_rollout? I vote preserve_rollout because it communicates intent to not silently override exposures.

Chen: agree. and we should add a read-only "fallback_history" to rollout object for the console to show example requests where fallback occurred.

Alex: good. I'll open an umbrella ticket and link sub tasks. linking the draft issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/4123 (WIP)

Lisa: I'll mock the UI for per-tier slider later today and drop in the ticket.

Sam: I'll prototype the runtime tiebreaker as a config flag in the router: `preserve_rollout_tiebreaker=true` and run perf tests.

ops-bot: noted. will create alert rule PR if telemetry is wired.

Maria: thanks team — let's sync next week after the prototype. :thumbsup:

Alex: thanks all. any objections to the plan?

Chen: no objections. one follow up: we should also document edge-case rollback semantics when a canary is scaled to 0 for a tier — ensure the rollout doesn't keep routing stale tokens.

Alex: good point — added to ticket.
